commands.title: GrantCellAuthorityLimit
commands.description: S0.1: actor is Underwriting Governance or senior executive - reference/configuration data, not transactional flow. OPEN QUESTION: is this purely internal (TFP governance), or does it require the capacity provider's own sign-off captured as part of the event?

events.title: CellAuthorityLimitGranted
events.description: S0.1: becomes the ceiling that all underwriter-level grants (S0.2) within that cell must fit inside.

events.title: UnderwriterAuthorityLimitGranted
events.description: S0.2: this is the record AssessSubmission (Context 2) checks against, via AuthorityMatrix.

readmodels.title: AuthorityMatrix
readmodels.description: The view Context 2's AssessSubmission actually queries at decision time. Renamed from an earlier generic 'AuthorityLimit' readmodel to match the terminology used once Context 0 was detailed - same underlying projection.

specifications.title: S0.2 Underwriter granted authority within cell's limit

commands.title: GrantUnderwriterAuthorityLimit
commands.description: S0.2/S0.3: Cell CUO granting authority to an individual underwriter, validated against the cell's own limit (S0.1). OPEN QUESTION: does validation need to account for other underwriters' existing grants - an aggregate pool per cell (sum of all underwriters can't exceed the cell's limit) vs. each underwriter's limit being independent (a per-transaction ceiling, not a shared pool)? Real domain question for governance stakeholders, not a technicality.

events.title: UnderwriterAuthorityLimitRejected
events.description: S0.3: requested delegation would exceed the cell's own limit. OPEN QUESTION: does rejection trigger escalation (a request to increase the cell's own overall limit, see CellAuthorityIncreaseRequested) or dead-end requiring the Cell CUO to reallocate existing underwriters' authority instead? Modeled the escalation path explicitly rather than leaving a pure dead end - see CellAuthorityIncreaseRequested.

specifications.title: S0.3 Underwriter authority request rejected - exceeds cell limit

commands.title: ReviseAuthorityLimit
commands.description: Either tier's authority record is revised - e.g. an annual treaty renewal resets the Cell's limit, or a Cell Head Underwriter adjusts an individual underwriter's delegation.

events.title: AuthorityLimitRevised
events.description: S0.4: sharpest open question in this context - a submission already in-flight (post-1a, pre-bind), assessed against the old limit, when the revision drops below what it needs. Grandfather (evaluate against authority in effect when it entered decisioning) vs re-evaluate (immediately re-check, force referral if it now breaches) are both defensible; leaning toward re-evaluation as the safer default for a governance-critical system, but this is a business decision, not an architecture default. Either way, always triggers ReassessInFlightSubmissionsOnRuleChange producing InFlightSubmissionReassessed, so the decision and its trigger are visible in the audit trail regardless of which policy stance is chosen. Same underlying 'rules changed mid-flight' problem as S1e.2's freeze-during-decisioning - solved with the same mechanism, not two bespoke ones.

specifications.title: S0.4 Authority limit revised downward mid-cycle
S0.4-err Revision attempted on a revoked authority

then.title: S0.4-err Revision attempted on a revoked authority
then.description: Authority limit has been revoked; it must be re-granted rather than revised.

commands.title: RevokeAuthorityLimit
commands.description: Either tier's authority record is revoked outright - e.g. an underwriter leaves the cell, or a Provider ends a Cell relationship for a class of business.

events.title: AuthorityLimitRevoked
events.description: S0.5: an underwriter with zero authority cannot have any submission proceed under their name, referral cascade or not - same in-flight question as S0.4 with sharper urgency, triggers ReassessInFlightSubmissionsOnRuleChange immediately. OPEN QUESTION: does revocation trigger a review flag on their recently bound business, similar to a thematic file review trigger? Not modeled as its own event yet - flagged for confirmation.

specifications.title: S0.5 Authority revoked entirely
S0.5-err Revoke attempted on an already-revoked authority

then.title: S0.5-err Revoke attempted on an already-revoked authority
then.description: Authority limit has already been revoked; a duplicate revocation is rejected.

events.title: CellAuthorityLimitGranted
events.description: Second instance of the same event type, paired here with the register projection it feeds.

readmodels.title: CellAuthorityRegister
readmodels.description: S0.1: current and historical authority limits per cell, queryable at any point in time.

specifications.title: S0.1 CellAuthorityRegister reflects the granted limit
S0.1 Cell granted a new authority limit
S0.1-empty No cells granted authority yet

commands.title: RequestCellAuthorityIncrease
commands.description: Escalation path from S0.3's rejection - modeled explicitly rather than a pure dead end, since in practice someone needs to know 'how do we actually get this underwriter the authority they need.'

events.title: CellAuthorityIncreaseRequested
events.description: S0.3 follow-on: loops back into a variant of S0.1 (GrantCellAuthorityLimit / AuthorityLimitRevised) if approved by the capacity provider/governance - the request itself is the auditable fact, distinct from whatever decision follows.

specifications.title: S0.3 follow-on: cell authority increase requested after rejection

events.title: UnderwriterAuthorityLimitGranted
events.description: Second instance of the same event type, paired here with the register projection it feeds (distinct from AuthorityMatrix, which is what Context 2 queries at decision time - this is the underwriter-facing historical register).

readmodels.title: UnderwriterAuthorityRegister
readmodels.description: S0.2: current authority per underwriter, with full history - distinct from AuthorityMatrix (the decision-time query view).

specifications.title: S0.2 UnderwriterAuthorityRegister reflects the grant

events.title: InFlightSubmissionReassessed
events.description: S0.4/S0.5's sharpest open question, generalized: what happens to a submission already in-flight when the rules it's being evaluated against change underneath it. Leaning toward re-evaluation as the safer default for a governance-critical system, but this is a business decision (policyApplied), not an architecture default. Revocation (S0.5) pushes for the stricter, immediate interpretation given it correlates with higher-risk situations; routine revisions (S0.4) may be more relaxed (checked at next decision point).

processors.title: ReassessInFlightSubmissionsOnRuleChange
processors.description: Triggered by AuthorityLimitRevised, AuthorityLimitRevoked (Context 0), and TerritoryUnderwritingFrozen (Context 1e) - one shared policy for 'rules changed mid-flight', not three separate reactive processes solving the same problem differently.

specifications.title: S0.4/S0.5 in-flight submission reassessed on authority change

commands.title: BindPolicy
commands.description: S3.1/S3.2: requires explicit underwriter confirmation, not fired automatically on QuoteAccepted - broker acceptance and the underwriter's final bind action are conceptually different moments (documentation checks, subjectivities being cleared).

events.title: PolicyBound
events.description: S3.1/S3.2: the immutable anchor for the policy's lifecycle - once fired, endorsements/cancellations append to history rather than rewriting this record. Everything downstream (Bordereaux in Context 4, Claims in Context 5) keys off it.

specifications.title: S3.1/S3.2 Policy bound, single or multi-provider allocation

commands.title: EndorsePolicy
commands.description: S3.3: broker-initiated change request, processed by the underwriter.

events.title: PolicyEndorsed
events.description: S3.3: fires for administrative changes directly. Material changes (premium/limit/exposure) instead produce EndorsementReferred if they exceed the underwriter's authority - resolves the open thread from S1c.3: an endorsement that increases exposure now goes through the same authority/referral check as an original bind, reusing Context 2's existing mechanism rather than a lightweight edit path that quietly bypasses governance.

specifications.title: S3.3 Administrative endorsement processed directly
S3.3-err Endorsement attempted on a cancelled policy

then.title: S3.3-err Endorsement attempted on a cancelled policy
then.description: Policy has been cancelled; a cancelled policy cannot be endorsed.

events.title: PolicyCancelled
events.description: S3.4: routine broker-requested or underwriter-initiated cancellation. Triggers the exposure reduction already modeled in S1c.4 - return premium calculation itself feeds Bordereaux/Settlement (Context 4), not computed here. For-cause cancellations use the separate PolicyCancelledForCause event instead, given the compliance/dispute implications of material misrepresentation.

specifications.title: S3.4 Routine policy cancellation
S3.4-err Cancellation attempted on an already-cancelled policy

then.title: S3.4-err Cancellation attempted on an already-cancelled policy
then.description: Policy has already been cancelled; a duplicate cancellation is rejected.

commands.title: InitiateRenewal
commands.description: S3.5: broker-initiated or system-prompted ahead of expiry. Renamed from RenewPolicy for clarity that this only initiates the loop, it doesn't itself bind anything.

events.title: PolicyRenewalInitiated
events.description: S3.5: 'loops back into a fresh submission/bind cycle, not shown as a literal loop on this timeline' - genuinely re-enters Context 1a/2 rather than a special renewal path. OPEN QUESTIONS (unresolved): does the new submission carry forward exposure/PML context from the expiring policy automatically, given Context 1c/1d/1e's exploratory status - flagged for later, but the linkage should exist even before those contexts are built. What happens if renewal is initiated but the broker doesn't respond before original expiry - lapse vs. grace/held-covered period is a real contractual question for underwriting stakeholders, not an architecture default.

specifications.title: S3.5 Renewal initiated ahead of expiry
S3.5-err Renewal attempted on a cancelled policy

then.title: S3.5-err Renewal attempted on a cancelled policy
then.description: Expiring policy has already been cancelled; there is nothing to renew.

events.title: PolicyBound
events.description: Second instance of the same event type, paired here with the register projection it feeds.

readmodels.title: PolicyRegister
readmodels.description: S3.1: the canonical current-state view of every bound policy.

specifications.title: S3.1 PolicyRegister reflects the bound policy

events.title: PolicyBound
events.description: Third instance of the same event type, paired here with the per-cell book-of-business projection it feeds.

readmodels.title: ActiveBookOfBusiness
readmodels.description: S3.1: per-cell view of currently active bound business.

specifications.title: S3.1 ActiveBookOfBusiness reflects the bound policy
S3.1-empty No bound policies yet for this cell

events.title: EndorsementReferred
events.description: S3.3: fires instead of PolicyEndorsed when a material change (premium/limit/exposure) exceeds the underwriter's authority - reuses Context 2's DecideReferral/ReferralApproved/ReferralDeclined resolution path rather than inventing a parallel one. Concrete example of the event model paying off architecturally: three contexts (Decisioning, Binding, and Context 0/1e's rule-change reassessment) now share one escalation mechanism instead of three bespoke ones.

specifications.title: S3.3 Material endorsement referred for authority check

events.title: PolicyCancelledForCause
events.description: S3.4: distinct from routine PolicyCancelled given the compliance/dispute implications of a for-cause cancellation (e.g. material misrepresentation discovered post-bind) - not just a different reason code on the same event.

specifications.title: S3.4 Policy cancelled for cause

events.title: BordereauDrafted
events.description: S4.1: draft bordereau created for a cell+provider+period. Becomes a real financial obligation only once agreed (see AgreeBordereau). Each line carries its own generated lineId (fixed per completeness check GAP-001).

processors.title: GenerateBordereauAutomation
processors.description: Scheduled period-close automation, scoped to one cell + one capacity provider + one period. Pulls together every policy transaction (bind/endorsement/cancellation) in that window not yet included in a prior bordereau.

specifications.title: S4.1 Period closes, bordereau drafted

events.title: BordereauLineQueried
events.description: Line status becomes Queried, independent of the bordereau's own overall status - each line tracks its own draft/queried/agreed state.

readmodels.title: BordereauDetail
readmodels.description: Working view of a bordereau and its lines for the provider/TPA review window - each line carries its own status (draft/queried/agreed/settled), not just the bordereau's overall status.

specifications.title: S4.2 Provider raises query on a bordereau line
S4.2 BordereauDetail reflects the queried line

commands.title: ResolveBordereauQuery
commands.description: Underwriter/Operations resolves a previously raised query.

events.title: BordereauLineResolved
events.description: Line status moves out of Queried. A single disputed line can span multiple periods before resolution.

specifications.title: S4.2 Query resolved, agreement can proceed

commands.title: AgreeBordereau
commands.description: Once every queried line is resolved, the capacity provider agrees the bordereau - this is the point it becomes a real financial obligation, not just a draft.

events.title: BordereauAgreed
events.description: S4.1/S4.2: only fires once BordereauSubmittedForAgreement has been confirmed by the provider AND zero queries remain open on the bordereau - by construction, since any query still open at period-close is resolved via BordereauLineResolved or excluded via BordereauLineDeferred before this point. No bordereau is ever agreed with a genuinely unresolved query still attached.

specifications.title: S4.1 Bordereau agreed by provider
S4.2-err Agreement attempted with an unresolved line query open

then.title: S4.2-err Agreement attempted with an unresolved line query open
then.description: One or more lines on this bordereau have an unresolved query; the bordereau cannot be agreed until every query is resolved or deferred.

commands.title: SettleBordereau
commands.description: Cash actually moves - net premium cell to provider (or claims float top-up provider to cell). Multi-currency: cell writes premium in local currency, providers may need it reported in USD, so FX rate at settlement is captured.

specifications.title: S4.1 Bordereau settled, cash moves
S4.1-err Settlement attempted before bordereau is agreed

then.title: S4.1-err Settlement attempted before bordereau is agreed
then.description: Bordereau has not yet been agreed by both provider and TFP; settlement cannot proceed before agreement.

commands.title: RaisePriorPeriodAdjustment
commands.description: An error found after a bordereau was already agreed is corrected via a new adjustment line in a future period - never by editing history. Bordereaux are an append-only ledger, mirroring the underlying policy transactions.

events.title: AdjustmentLineRaised
events.description: S4.4: the correction flows into next period's BordereauDrafted sweep as a new line - the original historical bordereau remains untouched, consistent with the immutable-ledger principle running through the whole model.

specifications.title: S4.4 Post-agreement correction via adjustment line

commands.title: SubmitBordereauForAgreement
commands.description: TFP finance/ops signals internal readiness - distinct from the provider's own confirmation (BordereauAgreed).

events.title: BordereauSubmittedForAgreement
events.description: S4.1: two-party agreement modeled as two events (BordereauSubmittedForAgreement -> BordereauAgreed) rather than one - TFP's internal sign-off is not the same fact as the provider's actual confirmation, and bordereaux are literally how money moves.

specifications.title: S4.1 Bordereau submitted for provider agreement

events.title: BordereauDrafted
events.description: Second instance of the same event type, paired here with the read model that determines what's swept into it.

readmodels.title: UnbilledTransactionsForPeriod
readmodels.description: S4.1: explicit link from each transaction to at most one bordereau (or none) - answers 'how does the system know a transaction hasn't already been included' as a queryable read model concern rather than an assumed fact.

specifications.title: S4.1 UnbilledTransactionsForPeriod reflects what's swept in
S4.1-empty No unbilled transactions for the period

commands.title: RaiseBordereauQuery
commands.description: Relocated here from its original column, where it had never actually landed on the grid due to the command/readmodel same-cell collision (BordereauDetail took the interaction cell there).

events.title: BordereauLineDeferred
events.description: S4.3: recommended default over blocking the whole bordereau - a single disputed line shouldn't hold up cash movement on everything else in the period. Mirrors the AdjustmentLineRaised pattern (S4.4) already established: a line rolls into a future period's draft, never editing history. This is what makes BordereauAgreed's 'zero open queries' rule always achievable by period-close - open queries are always either resolved or deferred before agreement, never left dangling.

processors.title: DeferQueriedLineAtPeriodClose
processors.description: Trigger: a BordereauLineQueried remains open as the period's normal processing timeline elapses.

specifications.title: S4.3 Unresolved line deferred to next period rather than blocking settlement

events.title: ClaimNotified
events.description: S5.1: notification may originate from broker/insured, but processing is the claims team's. References the original bind (and transitively the whole submission/decisioning lineage) via policyReference - a claims handler pulling up a claim gets the full PolicyOriginationView designed back in Search & Retrieval (1b.2).

screens.title: ClaimHandling
screens.description: Claims handler screen: violet header 'Claim CL-2026-0447'. A light-blue Policy Origination Lineage panel at top (pulled from Search & Retrieval) shows the submission-to-bind chain and the original bind terms (\$10,000,000 limit / \$185,000 premium). Below, claim details show date of loss and a loss description. A reserve-amount field shows \$4,500,000 next to a green checkmark reading 'Validated against bind terms'. Three buttons at the bottom: light-blue 'Set Reserve', green 'Pay Claim', and grey 'Close Claim'.

specifications.title: S5.1 Claim notified against a bound policy

events.title: ClaimReserveSet
events.description: S5.2: explicitly recurring - fires again whenever new information changes the loss estimate. A material increase crossing the claims handler's own authority threshold instead produces ReserveRevisionReferred - the authority/governance pattern from Context 0 isn't scoped only to underwriting decisioning, it applies here too.

specifications.title: S5.1/S5.2 Claim reserve set (recurring)
S5.2-err Reserve change attempted on a closed claim

then.title: S5.2-err Reserve change attempted on a closed claim
then.description: Claim is closed; reserve cannot be revised without first reopening the claim.

commands.title: PayClaim
commands.description: S5.1: validates the payment against the policy's limits/sub-limits/deductibles from the original bind terms - an explicit, visible step referencing PolicyOriginationView/bind terms directly, not just trusted to the claims handler's manual check. This is precisely the kind of governance point this system exists to make auditable rather than assumed.

events.title: ClaimPaid
events.description: S5.3: allocation mirrors the bind-time quota share automatically. OPEN QUESTION (unresolved, parallel to S0.1's per-provider question): could quota share change post-bind (novation, reinsurance restructure)? If so, this needs to reference whichever allocation was in effect at the relevant point, not blindly inherit the original split - would need point-in-time versioning like Context 0's authority model, not a simple lookup. Not resolved here.

specifications.title: S5.1/S5.3 Claim paid, split by provider quota share
S5.3-err Payment attempted on a closed claim

then.title: S5.3-err Payment attempted on a closed claim
then.description: Claim is closed; payment must reopen the claim first before further amounts can be paid.

specifications.title: S5.1 Claim closed
S5.1-err Close attempted on an already-closed claim

then.title: S5.1-err Close attempted on an already-closed claim
then.description: Claim has already been closed; a duplicate closure is rejected.

events.title: ClaimReopened
events.description: S5.4: appended after ClaimClosed, doesn't erase it - the same append-only 'corrections are new entries, not edits' principle used for Bordereaux (AdjustmentLineRaised) and Binding (PolicyEndorsed) applies here too, one architectural principle consistently applied rather than three separate decisions. Typically followed by a fresh ClaimReserveSet cycle. Reopen-limit/repeated-reopening-as-a-governance-signal not modeled yet - flagged as a natural extension, not essential day one.

specifications.title: S5.4 Claim closed then reopened

events.title: ClaimNotified
events.description: Second instance of the same event type, paired here with the register projection it feeds.

readmodels.title: ClaimRegister
readmodels.description: S5.1: the claim's permanent record, canonical current state.

specifications.title: S5.1 ClaimRegister reflects the notified claim
S5.1-empty No claims notified yet

events.title: ReserveRevisionReferred
events.description: S5.2: a material reserve increase crossing the claims handler's own authority threshold - genuine parallel to S3.3's endorsement/referral resolution. Suggests Context 0's authority engine is a cross-cutting capability (decisioning, endorsements, AND claims reserve authority), not something scoped only to Context 2 - worth reframing Context 0 as a general authority/governance engine rather than 'underwriting authority' specifically. Reuses the same DecideReferral resolution path as Context 2/Context 3's EndorsementReferred.

specifications.title: S5.2 Material reserve increase referred for authority check

events.title: ClaimNotifiedAgainstInactivePolicy
events.description: S5.5: fires when NotifyClaim references a policy whose current PolicyRegister state shows Cancelled or lapsed/non-renewed. Does NOT reject the notification - the loss may have occurred while cover was active. A flag, not a block.

specifications.title: S5.5 Claim notified against an inactive policy

commands.title: ValidateClaimPeriod
commands.description: Explicit human confirmation, not an automated pass/fail - date-of-loss-vs-active-period disputes (was the policy actually in force at the exact moment of loss, retroactive date issues) are exactly the kind of determination that ends up in coverage disputes and shouldn't be silently auto-decided.

events.title: ClaimPeriodValidated
events.description: S5.5: only required when ClaimNotifiedAgainstInactivePolicy has fired - a claims handler manually confirms the loss falls within the period on cover before reserve/payment proceeds.

specifications.title: S5.5 Claim period validated against date of loss

commands.title: SearchSubmissionHistory
commands.description: Used by underwriters (cell-scoped, 1b.1) and operations (broker-scoped, cross-cell, 1b.3) with the same shape, different searcherRole/scope. OPEN QUESTION (flagged by BA): is logging every search actually valuable, or over-engineering an audit trail for a read-only convenience feature? Leaning toward logging at the query level, not per-keystroke, given fast search-as-you-type UX. Also open: does free-text hit normalized ADEPT fields only, or raw broker documents too (a much bigger document-search problem)?

events.title: SubmissionHistorySearchPerformed
events.description: 1b.1: underwriter searches by risk attribute, scoped to their own cell by default (same authority-context mechanism as Context 0).

specifications.title: S1b.1 Underwriter searches submission history by risk attribute

events.title: SubmissionHistorySearchPerformed
events.description: Second instance of the same event type, paired here with the SubmissionSearchResults projection it feeds.

readmodels.title: SubmissionSearchResults
readmodels.description: Ranked/filtered list of matching historic submissions, each linking back to the full submission record including downstream decisioning/bind/claims history if it progressed that far.

specifications.title: S1b.1 SubmissionSearchResults reflects the search
S1b.1-empty Search finds no matching submissions

events.title: CrossCellSearchAttempted
events.description: 1b.4 permission-boundary design decision: default to cell-scoped visibility for underwriters (an underwriter in Aviation cannot by default see a submission that went to Energy for the same named insured), with cross-cell visibility as an explicit, logged, elevated permission for ops/governance (1b.3). Same audit-value reasoning as SubmissionRoutingRejected in Submission Intake - kept visible for whoever manages access policy, not just silently enforced. Possible middle ground worth exploring: a narrower 'same named insured, cross-cell' flag visible to underwriters without exposing full submission/pricing detail.

readmodels.title: BrokerActivityView
readmodels.description: 1b.3: all submissions from a given broker across all cells they're authorized for, with status breakdown - a cross-cell view ops needs for reconciliation even though individual underwriters don't for day-to-day work. Confirms Search & Retrieval needs at least two permission tiers baked in from day one (cell-scoped vs cross-cell), not a generic search with permission filtering bolted on afterward.

specifications.title: S1b.3 Operations searches a broker's history for reconciliation, cross-cell
S1b.4/1b.3 BrokerActivityView reflects the cross-cell search
S1b.3-empty No cross-cell activity found for broker in period

events.title: SubmissionLineageRetrieved
events.description: 1b.2, modeled deliberately as its own capability rather than folded into generic search (BA judgment call, agreed): a claims handler needing to verify a claim against original bind terms is a direct traversal by policy/bind reference, not a search over criteria. Likely one of the highest-value pieces of the whole 'AI-assisted search' capability described in the press coverage - solves exactly the 'days of manual reconstruction' problem.

readmodels.title: PolicyOriginationView
readmodels.description: Given a bound policy reference from a claim, the full chain: original submission -> decisioning path -> quote -> bind terms, without constructing a search query. Retrieved by policy/bind reference, not free-text search.

processors.title: RetrieveSubmissionLineageOnClaimNotified
processors.description: Triggered automatically whenever ClaimNotified fires (Context 5), not a manual search action - matches how claims handlers actually work.

specifications.title: S1b.2 Claims handler retrieves submission lineage for a bound policy
S1b.2 PolicyOriginationView reflects the retrieved lineage
S1b.2-empty No lineage found for an unbound submission

commands.title: ReceiveBrokerSubmission
commands.description: Renamed from SubmitBrokerSubmission - actor is the broker's system or Broker Connect's own ingestion service acting on the broker's behalf, not necessarily a direct user action. rawPayload is mapped to the ACORD standard schema (ADEPT) specifically - this is what enables automated data exchange across global broker systems generally, not a Howden-specific format, eliminating manual translation/mapping into internal databases.

events.title: BrokerSubmissionReceived
events.description: The raw receipt always succeeds if the payload arrives at all - always recorded regardless of what normalization/routing/duplicate-checking finds downstream. Class of business, territory, and other risk detail move to SubmissionNormalized once extraction succeeds.

specifications.title: S1a.1-err Submission received with no cell or class hint

then.title: S1a.1-err Submission received with no cell or class hint
then.description: Both cellIdHint and classOfBusinessHint are missing; submission cannot be routed for normalization without at least one.

events.title: SubmissionRoutingRejected
events.description: Broker's panel authorization doesn't cover the requested cell/class. Attempt is still recorded for broker relationship management - never silently dropped.

readmodels.title: BrokerAuthorizationExceptionLog
readmodels.description: Never appears in any underwriter's queue. Visible to whoever manages broker/cell panel relationships (ops or business development) - may represent a legitimate request to extend the broker's panel, not just an error.

specifications.title: S1a.3 Submission for a cell/class the broker isn't authorized for
S1a.3 BrokerAuthorizationExceptionLog reflects the routing rejection

events.title: SubmissionNormalized
events.description: ADEPT normalization succeeded - structured fields extracted from the raw payload. OPEN QUESTION (flagged by BA): is this genuinely a separate async event from BrokerSubmissionReceived, or should they collapse into one atomic event if normalization is synchronous/fast? Depends on actual ADEPT integration latency - revisit once that's known.

readmodels.title: SubmissionQueue
readmodels.description: Underwriter's main worklist. Possible-duplicate submissions stay in this normal flow with a badge (rather than a separate queue) since resolving them needs underwriter domain judgment, not just ops triage.

screens.title: SubmissionQueue
screens.description: Underwriter's Submission Queue screen: a violet header bar reads 'Submission Queue - itasca-mga' with a search input top-right. Below is a column-header row (Insured, Class, Line Size, Received, Status) over a divider line, followed by three submission rows: Acme Aviation Leasing Ltd (\$10.0M, Aircraft Non-Payment Credit) with a green 'Ready' badge; Meridian Port Holdings (\$25.0M, cat-exposed Property) with an orange 'Possible Dup' badge; and Blackstone Grid Energy LLC (\$8.5M, Energy Liability) with a green 'Ready' badge. A light-violet footer bar summarizes '3 submissions - 1 flagged as possible duplicate'.

specifications.title: Clean broker submission received and normalized
S1a.1 SubmissionQueue reflects the normalized submission
S1a.1 Clean broker submission received and normalized
S1a.1-empty No submissions currently queued

events.title: SubmissionNormalizationFailed
events.description: Missing required field, malformed data, unrecognized class code, or schema validation error. Raw payload is always preserved, never discarded. OPEN QUESTIONS (flagged by BA): (1) does the broker get an automatic notification, or is chasing manual - silent failure risks brokers bypassing the platform entirely; (2) is there a retry limit / timeout before a failed submission is considered abandoned?

readmodels.title: SubmissionExceptionQueue
readmodels.description: Separate from the underwriter's main queue - submissions stuck in a failed normalization state, for operations to chase the broker or manually intervene.

specifications.title: S1a.2 Submission received but fails ADEPT normalization
S1a.2 SubmissionExceptionQueue reflects the failed normalization
S1a.2-empty No failed normalizations outstanding

events.title: SubmissionManuallyCorrected
events.description: Manual remediation path: operations or the broker (re-sending) fixes the data, re-triggering normalization.

events.title: PotentialDuplicateSubmissionDetected
events.description: New submission is always recorded regardless (never silently dropped) - this event flags it as a possible resubmission alongside an existing open submission. OPEN QUESTION (flagged by BA): exact matching heuristic (exact-field vs fuzzy/probabilistic) materially affects false-positive rate and needs a real answer, not a placeholder.

specifications.title: S1a.4 Duplicate submission received

events.title: SubmissionSuperseded
events.description: Underwriter/ops confirms the new submission is a genuine resubmission/update of the original - modeled as its own linking event (old -> new) rather than silently discarding the original, preserving event-stream integrity.

events.title: SubmissionConfirmedDistinct
events.description: Underwriter/ops confirms the flagged submissions are coincidentally similar but genuinely distinct risks - both proceed independently.

events.title: BaselinePremiumGenerated
events.description: S1a.5: fires only on successful SubmissionNormalized - an incomplete/failed normalization shouldn't get a baseline price against partial data. Rating computation (EBM segmentation, satellite/weather cross-referencing) is a specialist capability this system requests and displays, never computes - same boundary discipline as ExportExposureExtract (1c.5) and PMLRecalculated (1d.2).

readmodels.title: PricedSubmissionView
readmodels.description: The broker's ask alongside the AI baseline, side by side, before the underwriter opens the file - this is what makes assessment 'auditing the AI-generated model' rather than pricing from scratch.

specifications.title: S1a.5 Baseline premium generated after successful normalization
S1a.5 PricedSubmissionView reflects the baseline alongside the broker's ask

events.title: PricingBaselineAccepted
events.description: Fires alongside AssessSubmission (S2.1) when the underwriter's proposedTerms match BaselinePremiumGenerated exactly. Actuarial needs to measure how often/how much underwriters deviate from the model to evaluate model performance - invisible unless captured explicitly, so this and PricingBaselineOverridden are modeled even though they add no new business decision by themselves.

specifications.title: S1a.5 Underwriter accepts the AI baseline as proposed

events.title: PricingBaselineOverridden
events.description: Fires alongside AssessSubmission when the underwriter's proposedTerms diverge from the baseline. Same model-feedback rationale as PricingBaselineAccepted.

specifications.title: S1a.5 Underwriter overrides the AI baseline

events.title: PricingModelVersionDeployed
events.description: Rapid model deployment ('quarters to hours' per TFP's own materials) means BaselinePremiumGenerated.modelVersion needs a real referent - this is that referent, audit reference data only.

specifications.title: S1a.5 New pricing model version deployed

events.title: SubmissionWithinAuthority
events.description: S2.1: submission moves from SubmissionQueue to a ready-to-quote state.

readmodels.title: AuthorityLimit
readmodels.description: Projection of the 3-tier authority cascade (Capacity Provider -> Cell -> Underwriter) used to validate an assessment. Populated by the Authority Administration slices (grant/revise/revoke).

screens.title: SubmissionAssessment
screens.description: Submission Assessment screen: violet header 'Assess Submission - Acme Aviation Leasing Ltd'. Two side-by-side panels below: a light-blue Submission panel (left) listing class, territory, proposed line size (\$10,000,000), premium (\$185,000), and effective date; a light-green Your Authority panel (right, versioned v3) showing the underwriter's limit (\$250,000 / \$15,000,000) against the proposed terms, a green checkmark reading 'Within authority', and a note that the freeze check passed. Two buttons at the bottom: green 'Approve & Quote' and light-red 'Decline'.

specifications.title: S2.1 Submission within authority, straight to quote

commands.title: AssessSubmission
commands.description: S2.1-S2.4: checked against both gates before the event fires - Context 0 (authority) and Context 1e (freeze). Per S1a.5, proposedTerms is now an adjustment of the AI-generated BaselinePremiumGenerated baseline (fires PricingBaselineAccepted or PricingBaselineOverridden alongside), not pricing from scratch.

events.title: SubmissionReferred
events.description: S2.2-S2.4: reused for every tier of a multi-level escalation, distinguished by parentReferralId.

specifications.title: S2.2/S2.4 Submission referred
S2.2-err Assessment attempted on an already-declined submission

then.title: S2.2-err Assessment attempted on an already-declined submission
then.description: Submission has already been declined; it cannot be re-assessed without first being resubmitted.

commands.title: DecideReferral
commands.description: S2.2/S2.3: resolving party approves, declines, or (if their own authority still doesn't cover it) implicitly triggers a further SubmissionReferred escalation.

events.title: ReferralApproved
events.description: S2.2: if termsModified, requires the original underwriter's acknowledgment (see ReferralTermsAcknowledged) before proceeding to quoting - they hold the broker relationship, so the referee doesn't unilaterally finalize terms the underwriter never actually offered.

specifications.title: S2.2 Referral approved at next tier

events.title: ReferralDeclined
events.description: S2.3: dead end for these specific terms, by this specific referee, for this specific authority reason - distinct from SubmissionDeclined (off-appetite entirely). Loops back to a fresh AssessSubmission with revised terms, not a hard stop - same submissionId persists (a revised assessment of the same underlying risk, same pattern as PolicyEndorsed being a new ledger entry on the same policy rather than a new one).

specifications.title: S2.3 Referral declined at next tier

commands.title: DeclineSubmission
commands.description: Underwriter declines a submission outright - off-appetite class, sanctioned territory, or incomplete information beyond a reasonable follow-up window.

events.title: SubmissionDeclined
events.description: S2.6: at any point in assessment, doesn't require a referral attempt first. Sanctioned-territory declines trigger ComplianceNotifiedOfSanctionsDecline - a mandatory downstream notification given the regulatory seriousness versus an ordinary off-appetite decline.

specifications.title: S2.6 Submission declined outright, off-appetite/sanctioned

commands.title: IssueQuote
commands.description: Once terms are within authority (directly or via approved referral), the underwriter issues a formal quote back to the broker. Not yet a bind.

events.title: QuoteIssued
events.description: S2.7: this is also the exact point S1e.2's freeze-block check applies - issuing a quote is the 'attempted action' intercepted if a freeze is active.

screens.title: QuoteView
screens.description: Broker's Quote screen: violet header 'Quote QT-2026-0912 - Howden'. A central light-violet card shows the insured (Acme Aviation Leasing Ltd), class (Aircraft Non-Payment Credit), line size (\$10,000,000), a large premium figure (\$185,000), and a validity note ('Valid until 2026-09-15, 14 days'). Three buttons below the card: green 'Accept Quote', yellow 'Request Amendment', and light-red 'Decline'.

specifications.title: S2.7 Quote issued
S2.7-err Quote issuance attempted on a declined submission

then.title: S2.7-err Quote issuance attempted on a declined submission
then.description: Submission has been declined; a quote cannot be issued against a declined submission.

commands.title: AcceptQuote
commands.description: Broker accepts the quote - this is what makes the submission eligible to bind. Modeled as its own event because a quote can also expire or be declined without binding.

events.title: QuoteAccepted
events.description: Submission is now eligible to bind.

specifications.title: S2.7 Quote accepted promptly
S2.7-err Accept attempted on an expired quote

then.title: S2.7-err Accept attempted on an expired quote
then.description: Quote's validity period has elapsed (QuoteExpired already recorded); acceptance after expiry is rejected.

commands.title: AcknowledgeReferralTerms
commands.description: S2.2: original underwriter acknowledges referee-modified terms before the submission proceeds to quoting.

events.title: ReferralTermsAcknowledged
events.description: Required whenever ReferralApproved.termsModified is true - the underwriter, not the referee, has final say on what actually gets offered to the broker.

specifications.title: S2.2 Original underwriter acknowledges modified referral terms

events.title: PendingReferralReassigned
events.description: S2.5: fires when AuthorityLimitRevoked (or Revised) removes the pending referral's resolving party's ability to act on it - rerouted to whoever now holds equivalent authority, rather than sitting unresolved against someone who can no longer act. Produced by ReassessInFlightSubmissionsOnRuleChange (Context 0) - same mechanism, third trigger.

specifications.title: S2.5 Pending referral reassigned after referee's authority revoked

events.title: PendingReferralHeld
events.description: S2.5: flagged for governance attention when no automatic reroute can be safely inferred (e.g. no clear equivalent-authority holder).

specifications.title: S2.5 Pending referral held for governance attention

events.title: ComplianceNotifiedOfSanctionsDecline
events.description: S2.6: mandatory downstream notification specifically for declineReasonCode=sanctioned-territory, given the regulatory seriousness versus an ordinary off-appetite decline.

specifications.title: S2.6 Compliance notified of sanctions-related decline

events.title: QuoteExpired
events.description: S2.8: submission moves to a closed/lapsed state distinct from decline - no one said no, it just wasn't taken up.

processors.title: ExpireStaleQuotes
processors.description: Scheduled/time-triggered policy, not a human command - runs when a quote's validity period elapses with no QuoteAccepted.

specifications.title: S2.8 Quote expires unaccepted

commands.title: DeclineQuote
commands.description: Broker-initiated, active decline rather than passive expiry.

events.title: QuoteDeclined
events.description: S2.9: kept distinct from QuoteExpired - an active decline (especially 'placed elsewhere') is genuinely useful competitive-intelligence data that passive expiry isn't.

specifications.title: S2.9 Broker explicitly declines the quote
S2.9-err Decline attempted on an already-accepted quote

then.title: S2.9-err Decline attempted on an already-accepted quote
then.description: Quote has already been accepted by the broker; a decline can no longer be recorded against it.

commands.title: RequestQuoteAmendment
commands.description: Broker-initiated.

events.title: QuoteAmendmentRequested
events.description: S2.10: triggers a fresh AssessSubmission pass against the amended terms - not a lightweight negotiation sub-flow. Amended terms could push the submission outside the underwriter's authority (e.g. higher line size requested), so it must go through the same Context 0/1e gate checks as any other assessment; a casual in-context negotiation would silently bypass both gates. Produces a fresh SubmissionWithinAuthority or SubmissionReferred, chained back to this event as prior context.

specifications.title: S2.10 Broker requests amended terms on an issued quote
